summary: The design-graph grammar: typed features with bounds and named faces, a compiler to CadQuery, part families as saved graphs (bracket first), and content hashes.

tasks.task: Define the grammar features and the compiler from design graph to CadQuery.
tasks.where: new files structura/grammar/features.py, structura/grammar/graph.py, structura/grammar/compile.py, tests/test_grammar.py
steps: 1. In features.py define one Pydantic schema per feature: plate, extrude_sketch, boss, hole, hole_pattern, rib, pocket, fillet, chamfer, shell, linear_pattern, circular_pattern, sweep_path, fin_array; each with parameters (unit, low, high), parent face reference and named output faces.
2. In graph.py define DesignGraph: ordered features, free-parameter list, validation that every parent reference exists and every value is inside its bounds.
3. In compile.py build the CadQuery solid feature by feature and return the solid plus a map from named faces to OCCT faces.
4. Write a test per feature that compiles it at the low and high corner of its bounds and checks for one valid solid.
5. Write a test that an out-of-bounds value or a missing parent fails validation before any geometry is built.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/test_grammar.py -q
tasks.done_when: Every feature compiles at its bound corners and invalid graphs are rejected before building.
do_not: do not expose a raw-code feature in the grammar
do not let compile() catch and hide CadQuery errors
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: a feature cannot compile at some in-bounds corner; then its bounds are wrong.

tasks.task: Define the template interface on top of graphs and the bracket family as a saved graph.
tasks.where: new files structura/templates/base.py, structura/templates/bracket.py, structura/families/bracket.json, tests/test_bracket_template.py
steps: 1. In base.py define Template: name, version, graph, free parameters (name, unit, low, high, default), build(params) -> solid, named_faces(shape) -> dict.

2. Write structura/families/bracket.json: plate with hole_pattern (two mounting holes), vertical plate, rib with linear_pattern, fillet; free parameters thickness, rib_count, rib_thickness, fillet_radius, plate_width.
3. bracket.py loads the JSON into a Template; named faces mount_holes, load_face, design_space.
4. Tests: default build is one valid solid, named faces are non-empty, out-of-bounds input raises with the parameter name.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/test_bracket_template.py -q
tasks.done_when: The bracket family builds from its graph for default and corner parameters with named faces.
do_not: do not hand-code bracket geometry in Python; it lives in the graph
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: a combination inside bounds gives an invalid solid.

tasks.task: Store each design as graph, parameters and hash.
steps: 1. Define Design (template name, template version, graph, params, created_at) with a sha256 hash over the canonical graph JSON and params rounded to 6 significant digits.
2. design.save(dir) writes graph.json, params.json and the compiled CadQuery script; load(dir) restores it.
3. Test that equal graphs and params give equal hashes and any change gives a new hash.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/test_designs.py -q
tasks.done_when: Designs round-trip through disk with stable hashes.
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the hash differs between two runs with equal inputs.

acceptance: Every grammar feature compiles at its bound corners
Bracket family defined only as a graph
risks: The grammar grows without end; the first release is the fourteen features listed and new ones need an owner decision.
Fillets fail on thin ribs; bounds keep fillet radius below half the rib thickness and the gate (B4) repairs the rest.
